Version 1.1 |accessdate=24 August 2015}} }} '''''Phyllostachys aurea''''' is a species of [[bamboo]], and is of the 'running bamboo' type, belonging to the diverse [[Bambuseae]] tribe. It is native to [[Fujian]] and [[Zhejiang]] in [[China]]. It is commonly known by the names '''fishpole bamboo''', '''golden bamboo''', '''monk's belly bamboo''', and '''fairyland bamboo''' (Australia). ==Cultivation== ''Phyllostachys aurea'' is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]] for gardens. In the United States, Australia, South Africa and Italy, it is considered an invasive species that crowds out native species and becomes a [[monoculture]] that is difficult to remove.{{cite web | url = https://www.cabi.org/isc/datasheet/42072 | title = Invasive Species Compendium: "Phyllostachis aurea | publisher = [[Centre for Agriculture and Bioscience International|CABI]] | access-date = 14 July 2021}} It is a cold-hardy bamboo, performing well in USDA zones 6 to 10, (Connecticut to Florida).{{cite web |url= http://www.capemaybamboo.com/GOLDEN-BAMBOO.html |title= Cape May Bamboo - ''Phyllostachys Aurea'' (Golden Bamboo) |accessdate= 2014-01-17 |archive-date= 2014-02-21 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20140221184504/http://www.capemaybamboo.com/GOLDEN-BAMBOO.html |url-status= dead }} In the UK it has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Phyllostachys aurea'' | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/75274/Phyllostachys-aurea/Details | access-date = 6 February 2021}}{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 78 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 25 April 2018}} It is a tall [[evergreen]] species growing to {{convert|8|m|ft|abbr=on}} tall by {{convert|4|m|ft|abbr=on}} broad. Like most bamboos it can become invasive if kept in warm, moist conditions in good quality soil with access to full sunlight. It is a prohibited species in New York. ===Cultivars=== Cultivars include: * ''P. aurea'' 'Flavescens Inversa' – some lower [[culm (botany)|culms]] may show a pale yellow stripe on the [[Sulcus (morphology)|sulcus]] * ''P. aurea'' 'Holochrysa' – common name "golden golden", culms turn yellow/gold sooner than the type form, random leaves have a yellow stripe * ''P. aurea'' 'Koi' – culms turn yellow, but sulcus stays green, random leaves have a yellow stripe * ''P. aurea'' 'Takemurai' – culms grow taller and lack the compressed [[Internode (botany)|internodes]] of the type form ==Uses== ''P. aurea'''s lush foliage makes it desirable for ornamental purposes and privacy hedges, and its characteristic 'knotty' compressed lower internodes render it desirable among collectors. It is well-suited to the making of [[Bamboo_musical_instruments|bamboo pipe]]s. ==Identification and growth habit== [[File:Golden_Bamboo_(Phyllostachys_Aureosulcata)_Compressed_Internodes.jpg|thumb|right|Compressed internodes with tortoiseshell-like appearance]] The common forms of ''P. aurea'' are easily identified by their characteristic compressed internodes in the lower part of the canes which have a tortoise shell-like appearance. This internodal compression result in shorter heights (25 ft) and thicker cane diameters (relative to height) than many other ''Phyllostachys'' species. The canes turn yellow in full or partial sun, and deepen into a gold-orange color as the plant matures. Branching and foliage tend to start lower to the ground than many other ''Phyllostachys'' species, but some prefer to cut off lower branches to show off the interesting 'tortoise shell' lower part of the canes. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons category-inline|Phyllostachys aurea|''Phyllostachys aurea''}}
